Passive ground emitter location techniques are vital to electronic warfare system (EWS) providing threat warnings in hostile environments. The paper focuses on proposing and evaluating solutions for optimizing the UAV trajectories for localization of a RF emitter using Line of Bearing (LOB) measurements. The optimization approach aims to minimize the size of the target position error ellipse. A framework using only the geometry of the problem is explored to minimize the maximal bounds of the emitters’ locations without using a belief or probability distribution needed for iterative approaches, which requires a good initial guess to ensure convergence on the true position. The effectiveness of the geometric approach is shown by designing and evaluating a global decision-making strategy based on Learning Real-Time A* (LRTA*) algorithm. Through simulations, the search solution is compared to a conventional optimal control solution approach for a two dimensional space case. The LRTA* solution achieves acceptable accuracy with sufficient observation points and it is suitable for real-time purposes. The solution is also attractive for its capability to initialize iterative algorithms if needed.

articleTitle: Performance analysis of quadcopter drones to radar detection and track initialization characteristics optimization
abstract: The main contribution of this preliminary study is the determination and risk evaluation of the homemade quadcopter drone’s performance characteristics from an anti-drone system point of view. The preliminary expectations of the quadcopter mechatronics engineering design challenges are reviewed. The magnitude changes of radar cross-section using the micro-Doppler effect of homemade drone development variations are investigated for further improvement criteria of radar detection and track initialization optimization. The quadcopter detectability of the hovering and maneuvering circumstances is demonstrated with simplified but state-of-the-art requirements.

articleTitle: Concurrent Activity Classification and Human Identification Based on Point Cloud Data and Deep Learning
abstract: Human sensing has long been an actively studied problem due to its potential in a wide range of applications. However, most existing approaches depend on cameras that require proper light condition and also pose quite a challenge for privacy protection due to native nature of easy understanding by eyes in the visual data. As a promising alternative, mmWave radars have been explored recently as a viable alternative to provide precise human sensing capability without aforementioned concerns. In this paper, we propose to use commercial low-cost mmWave radars to perform multiple human sensing functionalities concurrently and accurately based on a multi-task learning architecture. We show that the proposed system is able to classify activities and identify human individuals at the same time such that question of “Who is doing what” can be asked. Our experiments show that an average accuracy of 98.4% and 97.6% are achieved respectively for the two tasks by the proposed method, implying its great potential for effective human sensing using mmWave radars.

articleTitle: Real-Time Video SAR on Curved Trajectories Making Use of Graphic Core Processing
abstract: This paper provides a video SAR processing scheme with flexible trajectories along with a brief introduction of the corresponding SAR backprojection approach. For this processing algorithm a Matlab model is introduced and respective aspects for acceleration and robustification of the method are presented, making use of graphic core processing. A processing example of $4096\times 4096$ image pixels with 16384 antenna positions is evaluated with which an acceleration factor of more than 430 is achieved compared to a Matlab implementation. Results of the backprojection implementation are provided with real flight data, acquired using HENSOLDT’s Multifunction Surveillance Radar PrecISR™ 1000 and compared to an $\omega$-k algorithm. A first example of a video SAR processing is finally presented.

articleTitle: Calibration of Large Coherent MIMO Radar Arrays: Channel Imbalances and 3D Antenna Positions
abstract: One of the main challenges for next generation automotive radars is the improvement of angular resolution to a sub-degree level. In this context, wide aperture automotive radars of 1m length or more and resolution close to 0.1° in azimuth and 0.5° in elevation could be beneficial. To enable coherent processing of arrays with such large aperture, prior (i.e offline) and online calibration are necessary: channel imbalances (gains and phases) and three dimensional coordinates of transmit and receive elements need to be determined. We propose a calibration strategy based on alternating steps between the two subtasks of i) channel imbalance estimation with ‘known’ array positions, by applying a singular value decomposition to the resulting tensor calculus problem; and ii) antenna position estimation with ’known’ channel imbalances, by numerically maximizing the Bayesian posterior probability; in both cases operating on range/Doppler snapshots of disjoint targets (with potentially unknown locations). Simulation studies based on the parameters of a MIMO 8x6 linear sparse array show promising results as long as the initial position errors do not exceed half a wavelength (2mm), beyond which we observe strong effects of ambiguity. Experimental results with real measurements show that after calibration in laboratory conditions, our MIMO 8x6 demonstrator with 50cm aperture is able to resolve two targets at the same range with angular separation at least as close as 0.4°.
